summary: Memoization saves the result of each method call so the same input is never computed twice. It turns naive recursive Fibonacci from exponential time into linear time.
notes: memo.containsKey(n) checks for a saved answer before doing any work.
Map<Integer, Long> uses wrapper types because generics cannot hold int or long directly.
long is exact up to fib(92). fib(93) overflows and wraps to a negative number, and every value after it is wrong.
pitfall: Using memo.computeIfAbsent(n, k -> fibMemo(k - 1) + fibMemo(k - 2)) on a HashMap changes the map while it is being updated and throws ConcurrentModificationException. Use containsKey, get, and put.
